newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Vienna-Warsaw express derails in Czech flooding.
newsitem.headline: Vienna-Warsaw express derails in Czech flooding.

text.p: A Vienna-Warsaw express train derailed into floodwaters near Ostrava in the Czech Republic on Monday and the official news agency CTK said 64 passengers were injured.
Flooding from torrential rain since the weekend was believed to have killed a total of five people in the central European country, CTK said in a separate report.

CTK quoted an Ostrava police spokewoman as saying that several cars from the derailed train were underwater and more injured people might be found. Some rail cars came to rest as far as 500 metres (1,650 feet) from the tracks.
"There was a (train) accident between Ostrava and Prerov and it was most probably a result of the floods," ministry spokesman Petr Stahlavsky told Reuters.
He said the Eurocity express jumped the tracks shortly before 1 p.m. (1100 GMT) but could not confirm CTK's report of injuries and had no further details.
The northeastern region around Ostrava has been inundated by rain since Sunday, causing rivers and tributaries to spill over their banks and putting low-lying areas under water.
Rail and road service to parts of the region has been suspended. Czech officials issued calls for drinking water and emergency supplies as rivers to continue to rise.

Two women and three men were believed to have died from the flooding which has swept away houses and cut off dozens of people from rescue crews, CTK said. Marooned residents had to scramble onto their rooftops.
Numerous towns and villages lining tributaries to the Opava and Morava rivers have been swamped.
Hundreds of people, including children attending summer camps near the rising waters, have been evacuated, and rail and road transport suspended in some nearby areas.
Roads, electricity, and telephone service has been disrupted in many parts of the northeast and sources of drinking water have been tainted by the rising tide.

"I would ... ask all who can offer help to give whatever volume of drinking water, in whatever packaging, in tanks or in bottles," Ladislav Olejnicek, spokesman for the flood crisis team, told Czech radio.
Some hospitals lost their potable water, CTK said, and the waterworks in Ostrava was cut off from several sources.
Disaster relief officials declared a state of emergency and the government dispatched helicopters, soldiers, police and fire units from around the country to aid rescue operations.

Forecasts throughout much of the region were for more heavy rain in the next 24 hours, threatening low-lying regions including Ostrava, the country's third largest city, and the industrial town of Zlin further downstream.
Officials feared flooding could start affecting tributaries of the Elbe and Upa rivers in the eastern Bohemia region.
Early damage estimates have already topped the two billion crowns ($62 million) incurred by flooding in the same region last year. ($ = 32.25 Czech Crowns)
